    Chaos Game

    Fraction of the way each point jumps toward a random vertex. Around 0.5 fills the polygon; lower values open fractal gaps.

    Formula Sandbox GLSL

    A custom formula controls this fractal's iteration step.
    Write the body of customIter(z, c); return next z as vec2. Available: cmul, cdiv, cpow, cexp, clog, csin, ccos, csqrt, cabs. Avoid unbounded loops (while(true) / for(;;)). GLSL can't time them out, so they may freeze the GPU; reload the tab to recover.

    3D DE Sandbox GLSL

    A custom formula controls this fractal's surface shape.
    Write a body for float DE(vec3 p) returning distance to nearest surface. Default: Mandelbulb power 8. Variables in scope: p. Bounded loops are fine; avoid unbounded ones (while(true)). They can freeze the GPU, so reload the tab if it hangs.

    Buddhabrot

    Details
    More samples = finer nebula detail (slower). v6.0.8: cap raised 4M → 10M for serious print-quality density work; cancel via the render pill if a high-sample run gets long.
    Higher = remove fast-escaping boundary noise

    Attractor Parameters

    How the attractor's shape shifts as you adjust its coefficients.
    These coefficients define the attractor's equations, and their labels change with the attractor type. Small changes near the defaults keep the shape recognizable; large ones can collapse or transform it.

    Metatron's Cube
    Fruit of Life
    The densest way to pack spheres in 3D.
    3D = the densest 3D sphere-packing nucleus (1 center + 12 cuboctahedron vertices). Buckminster Fuller called this the "Vector Equilibrium". The 2D figure is its hexagonal projection.
    Egg of Life
    Eight spheres touching at a shared center point.
    3D = 8 spheres at cube vertices, all touching at the body-center (Drunvalo Melchizedek's canonical 3D Egg).
    Flower of Life
    Nineteen spheres stacked in one tightly packed layer.
    3D = the canonical 19-sphere figure as a single hex-close-packed layer; rotation reveals the lattice structure.
    Fibonacci Lattice / Sphere
    Points spread evenly across a sphere's surface.
    3D = N points on the unit sphere via golden-angle spiral. Used in cosmology, ML embedding init, and irradiation modeling for its near-uniform spherical distribution.
    Phyllotaxis (sphere)
    The same spiral spread as the Fibonacci sphere, with an adjustable angle.
    3D = same construction as Fibonacci sphere, but tunable: 137.508° = uniform · 137.4° / 137.6° = visible parastichy bands. Phyllotaxis panel above controls angle + dot size.
    Vesica Piscis
    Off = nested rosette of S.layers pairs (decorative)
    Hyperbolic {p,q}
    Need 1/p + 1/q < 1/2. {7,3}, {6,4}, {8,3}, {5,4} all work.
    Elementary CA
    30 = chaotic (Wolfram PRNG) · 90 = Sierpiński · 110 = Turing-complete · 184 = traffic
    Indra's Pearls (Maskit slice μ)
    Shifts the pattern between a solid interior and a torn, fractal edge.
    μ ≈ 1.5+0.5i = quasi-Fuchsian interior (default). 1.91+0.05i = near the real-axis Apollonian cusp. 2+0i = Apollonian cusp. 0+2i = degenerate vertical cusp. Below the discreteness boundary the limit set tears apart.
    Polyhedron Display
    Off = wireframe (default). On = depth-sorted faces with Z-fade.
    4D Projection
    Two ways to flatten a 4D shape into 3D · pick whichever reads more clearly for this shape.
    Schlegel = the classic nested "cube-in-cube" edge graph (flattens one cell to a frame) · Stereographic = round pole-projection from the 4-sphere. Simple convex polytopes open in Schlegel; the dense 120/600-cell and star polytopes open in stereographic. (Also reachable via ?schlegel.)
    Modulates auto-rotation through the xw / zw planes when geometry animation is on.
    Torus Knot (p, q)
    How many times the knot winds around the tube before it closes.
    p comes from the Layers slider · (2,3) = trefoil · (2,5) = cinquefoil · (3,4)/(3,5) = denser knots · gcd(p,q)>1 yields a torus link
    Quasicrystal
    Symmetry with no repeating tile, the same idea as a Penrose tiling.
    5 = 10-fold (Penrose-style) · 6 = 12-fold (dodecagonal) · 4 = 8-fold (octagonal) · all crystallographically forbidden, quasi-periodic
    Conic Section
    0 = circle · 0<e<1 = ellipse · 1 = parabola · e>1 = hyperbola
    Cassini Ovals
    <1 = two ovals · =1 = lemniscate of Bernoulli · >1 = single oval
    Möbius Strip
    How many half-twists the strip has before it closes.
    1 = canonical Möbius (non-orientable) · 2 = cylinder (orientable double-cover) · odd k = (k/2)-twist Möbius
    Klein Bottle
    Scales the figure-8 cross-section · 1.0 = canonical immersion
    Parabolic String Art
    4 = square (legacy) · 3 = triangular · 5 = pentagonal · 6 = hexagonal envelopes
    Just-Intonation Lattice
    Which set of pure musical intervals the lattice is built from.
    5-limit = canonical Western just intonation (3·5 axes) · 7-limit adds septimal/blues intervals (7/4 harmonic seventh, 7/6 septimal third)
    Recamán's Sequence
    More terms show more of the sequence's long-term pattern.
    More terms reveal the long-range "is every integer hit?" question's empirical density (Sloane's open problem)
    Poincaré Disk
    4 = legacy (0°/45°/90°/135°) · 2 = simple cross-hatch · 6 = dense hyperbolic web
    Domain Coloring
    A custom shader formula controls this pattern's shape.
    GLSL ES 3.00 · return a vec2. Available: z (vec2 input), cmul(a,b), cdiv(a,b), u_N (int), u_rot, u_tau (vec2). The formula is checked before it reaches the shader, and it needs WebGL2 (there is no CPU fallback).
    Colors show the complex function's phase and magnitude directly.
    Phase plot of f:ℂ→ℂ. Hue = arg f(z), brightness = log|f(z)|. Zeros are black rosettes; poles white rosettes; essential singularities Picard-chaotic. Degree applies to zn − 1 and Blaschke; rotation feeds Möbius/Blaschke. SSAA smooths branch cuts at N²× cost. Auto-rotate animates the function-parameter rotation (Möbius / Blaschke a-points). 3D lift renders a height-mapped Riemann surface; drag to rotate, height = log1p|f(z)|. Reference: Wegert 2012.
    Composite Polyhedron
    Renders two named solids simultaneously.
    Gray-Scott Parameters
    Feed and kill rates shape spots, stripes, or other reaction-diffusion textures.
    F=0.037, k=0.060 = spots · F=0.029, k=0.057 = stripes · F=0.014, k=0.054 = u-skate
    Lenia Dynamics
    Controls that keep the pattern inside its stable, lifelike range.
    μ = preferred density · σ = growth width · R = kernel size. Lenia lives in a narrow band; these ranges stay inside it.
    Gierer–Meinhardt Decay
    Balances spot versus stripe patterns in the reaction-diffusion simulation.
    Activator (μₐ) / inhibitor (μₕ) decay, the spot-vs-stripe balance. Gierer–Meinhardt lives in a narrow band near these defaults: lower μₐ → bolder blobs, higher μₕ → finer texture.
    Spectre Monotile
    0 = straight-edged tile · 0.15 = canonical curved Spectre · higher = stronger zig-zag
    Mandala
    Offsetting alternate bands is what makes the pattern interlock rather than align.
    Alternates with the motif above, position by position. An odd count leaves one seam.
    A heavy outer border around fine inner bands is most of what reads as intricate.
    Radial ties running inward to the next band. 0 leaves the gap open.
    Blends each element toward its cardinal color: white east, yellow south, red west, green north. Applies to every band.
    L-System Preset
    Axiom
    Rules one per line: X = production
    Turtle: F/G draw forward · +/− turn · [/] push/pop. Try axiom F, rule F=F[+F]F[-F]F, angle 25.7° for a tree.

    Stroke & Fill

    Set either to 0 for a fill-only silhouette
    Solid: one unbroken stroke.
    Dash tuning
    Scales the preset above. Gap at 0 renders solid.
    Slides the dash along the path to register marks against vertices. Keyframeable in Motion Studio.
    Round: each mark ends in a semicircle. Extends every mark by half the line weight at both ends.
    Round: corners are arcs. Softest, and the safest at heavy line weights.
    Off: draw strokes only.
    This pattern draws strokes only, so fill has no effect on it.
    Nonzero: any region the path winds around is filled. Overlaps read as one solid body.
    How overlapping fills combine. Multiply turns overlap into structure.
